phase6_6_discrepancy_reconciliation.technical_root_cause: In Phase 6.6, failure timestamps were reconstructed solely from windows with label > 0. Entities 6224307516_2 and 6224307516_3 experienced repeated failures (at t=9232.6 and t=13367.6 for task 2; and t=9455.5 and t=13367.6 for task 3). Between t=9300 and t=10200, 7 normal windows were observed with time_to_failure between 3167.6s and 4259.3s (> 30 min) preceding the second failure. Because telemetry for these tasks halted after t=10200, no Warning or Critical windows (label > 0) were generated for the second failure. Consequently, Phase 6.6 omitted the second failure timestamp, erroneously classifying these 7 windows as 'post-failure' rather than 'pre-failure'. Ground-truth raw event auditing proves the correct breakdown is exactly 147 pre-failure normal windows and 149 post-failure normal windows (discrepancy = 7 windows).

evidence_classifications.claim_description: False alarms are overwhelmingly Critical alerts (73.1% to 97.1%) rather than Warning alerts.
evidence_classifications.interpretation: Confirmed exactly. Models systematically bypass intermediate Warning states when triggering false positives.

evidence_classifications.claim_description: Missing CPI telemetry (cpi_missing_fraction_6) exhibits extreme positive elevation (Cohen's d +1.21 to +2.95) among false positives in pure-normal entities.
evidence_classifications.interpretation: Confirmed mathematically with entity-cluster bootstrap. Qualification: This is strictly an observational association. It cannot establish that missing telemetry causes false alarms or task failure; it reflects correlation with crash telemetry in training data.

evidence_classifications.claim_description: Three parent jobs account for 50% to 61% of all false positive windows in Random Forest and Compact Transformer.
evidence_classifications.denominator: 112 parent jobs with primary normal windows

independent_result.temporal_lstm: Top 3 jobs generate 602 of 1,293 FPs (46.56%); Top 4 jobs generate 54.52%
independent_result.representation_hybrid: Top 3 jobs generate 554 of 1,667 FPs (33.23%); Top 7 jobs generate 50.27%

evidence_classifications.interpretation: Confirmed for Random Forest and Compact Transformer. Qualification: Job-exclusion sensitivity analysis is post-hoc and selection-biased; it does not indicate expected performance in production deployment.

evidence_classifications.claim_description: Failing-cohort normal windows partition into exactly 140 pre-failure normal windows and 156 post-failure recovery windows.
evidence_classifications.interpretation: Disproved. Ground-truth lifecycle event auditing reveals 147 pre-failure normal windows and 149 post-failure windows. Phase 6.6 misclassified 7 windows because it reconstructed failure timestamps solely from label > 0 windows, missing a subsequent failure episode that lacked pre-failure telemetry.

evidence_classifications.claim_description: Sequence models detect pre-failure degradation 30 to 48 minutes in advance, causing 75% to 98% false alarm rates on pre-failure normal windows.
evidence_classifications.denominator: 147 verified pre-failure normal windows (tau > 30 min before failure)
evidence_classifications.interpretation: Empirically supported on corrected denominators (74.8% - 94.6%). Qualification: The claim that this represents 'genuine physical degradation' remains an unverified hypothesis; current telemetry cannot establish physical health without external kernel logs.

evidence_classifications.claim_description: Under uniform argmax in a 3-class problem, models trigger Critical alerts with predicted probabilities as low as 0.336 to 0.359 whenever P(0) drops below 0.34.
evidence_classifications.interpretation: Confirmed mathematically. In a 3-class system, argmax selects Critical as long as P(2) > P(0) and P(2) > P(1), which occurs at P(2) ≈ 0.34 when classes 0 and 1 are evenly split.

evidence_classifications.claim_description: In Compact Transformer, uncalibrated training forced the network into extreme saturation on false positives (median P(Critical) = 0.993).
evidence_classifications.denominator: 904 Critical false positive windows in Compact Transformer
evidence_classifications.interpretation: Confirmed exactly. Compact Transformer exhibits severe probability overconfidence on false alarms due to uncalibrated softmax outputs.

evidence_classifications.claim_description: All four models were trained with ~10x loss weights on Critical and ~13x on Warning.
evidence_classifications.interpretation: Disproved. Only Random Forest and Hybrid used balanced weighting (~11.5x and ~17.0x). The neural sequence models (LSTM and Transformer) were trained with explicit weights [1.0, 1.5, 2.0]. The claim that neural models had 10x loss weighting is factually incorrect.

evidence_classifications.claim_description: Missing CPI telemetry causes task failure or represents causal degradation.
evidence_classifications.denominator: Google cluster trace telemetry and kernel logs
evidence_classifications.independent_result: Trace data lacks kernel interrupt logs, CPU scheduler profiling, and hardware counter fault events.
evidence_classifications.interpretation: Cannot be verified from available observational telemetry. Missing CPI counters may reflect benign thread idling, Borg scheduler descheduling, or collection pauses.

unresolved_limitations: Causal status of CPI missingness cannot be determined without physical machine profiling logs.
Whether pre-failure normal alerts represent genuine degradation or spurious drift cannot be confirmed without kernel dmesg logs.
True operational deployment performance cannot be known without testing on a newly sampled cohort.
required_next_experiment_evidence: Decision thresholds must be pre-registered using cost-sensitive utility optimization on development validation data.
Cross-entropy loss weights must be systematically tuned via validation grid search rather than ad-hoc selection.
Missing telemetry indicators must be isolated from continuous resource utilization signals.
Evaluations must be conducted on an untouched holdout from independent time periods or distinct datacenters.
